items.text: Notice the entry small talk gives you and go deep.
Instead of just bouncing from topic to topic in a wide conversation, start learning how to have deeper conversations.
Deeper conversations are always finding new layers inside the topic that you have already got, rather than always looking for new topics.
Adding one more sentence is probably the easiest way to make your conversations more interesting.
When you're answering somebody's question, just tell yourself to add one more sentence to give them a way to start a good new fun conversation.
When you're the one asking the questions, don't just rapid-fire ask them, because that is just simply question, answer, question, answer.
Before asking another question, try adding one more sentence.
React to what they meant, not just what they said.
Try and find the meaning underneath what you think they're trying to communicate to you.
Don't just listen to the information that people are always giving you; instead, sometimes ask yourself why they are telling you this and what the deeper meaning behind it is.
Stop exchanging facts and instead ask for opinions, because facts will just tell you what's happened, but opinions will tell you what people actually think about what has happened.
You can also do this by flipping this around and asking for their opinion to actually start finding what they actually like.
Stop trying to make every conversation deep.
If you try going a little bit deeper and they say nothing really particularly exciting, it is okay to leave the conversation topic how it is and move on to the next one.
If you mention a new topic and they suddenly engage with it, that is exactly where you stay in the conversation and go a little bit deeper.
